cases.sentence: К тебе поднимаю ___ свои, обитающие на небесах.
cases.translation: I lift my eyes to you, who sit enthroned in heaven.
cases.explain: The transitive verb поднимаю (lift) governs the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Вот как глаза слуг смотрят на ___ своего господина.
cases.translation: As servants look to the hand of their master.
cases.explain: The transitive verb смотрят (look to) governs the accusative case.

cases.translation: As a maid looks to the hand of her mistress.
cases.explain: The preposition на (to/upon) in this context takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Так наши глаза обращены на ___, до тех пор, пока Он не смилуется.
cases.translation: So our eyes look to the Lord, until He is merciful to us.
cases.explain: The preposition на (to/upon) takes the accusative case.

cases.translation: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us.
cases.explain: The transitive verb помилуй (have mercy on) governs the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Душа наша наполнена до краев ___ надменных.
cases.translation: Our soul is filled with the scorn of the proud.
cases.explain: The instrumental of means indicates what fills the soul.

reading.ru: К тебе поднимаю глаза свои, обитающие на небесах.
reading.question: To whom does the psalmist lift his eyes?
options: To God who dwells in heaven
reading.correct: To God who dwells in heaven
reading.explain: The opening verse shows: К тебе поднимаю глаза свои, обитающие на небесах — I lift my eyes to you, who are enthroned in heaven.

reading.ru: Вот как глаза слуг смотрят на руку своего господина, и глаза служанки на руку своей госпожи.
reading.question: What analogy does the psalmist use to describe his watching?
options: Servants watch their master's hand, maids watch their mistress's hand
reading.correct: Servants watch their master's hand, maids watch their mistress's hand
reading.explain: The comparison is explicit: глаза слуг смотрят на руку своего господина (servants' eyes watch their master's hand), и глаза служанки на руку своей госпожи (and maids' eyes watch their mistress's hand).

reading.ru: Так наши глаза обращены на Господа, до тех пор, пока Он не смилуется над нами.
reading.question: Where are the psalmist's eyes turned, and for how long?
options: Turned to the Lord until He shows mercy
reading.correct: Turned to the Lord until He shows mercy
reading.explain: The verse states: Так наши глаза обращены на Господа, до тех пор, пока Он не смилуется над нами — So our eyes look to the Lord our God, till he shows us his mercy.

reading.ru: Помилуй нас, Господи, помилуй нас, потому что мы по горло насыщены презрением.
reading.question: Why does the psalmist ask for mercy?
options: Because they are filled to overflowing with contempt
Because they are poor and hungry
Because they are sick and weak
Because they are far from home
reading.correct: Because they are filled to overflowing with contempt
reading.explain: The reason given is: потому что мы по горло насыщены презрением — because we have endured no end of contempt (literally 'we are filled to the throat with contempt').

reading.ru: Душа наша наполнена до краев оскорблением надменных и презрением гордых.
reading.question: What has filled the psalmist's soul?
options: The insult of the arrogant and contempt of the proud
reading.correct: The insult of the arrogant and contempt of the proud
reading.explain: The verse describes: Душа наша наполнена до краев оскорблением надменных и презрением гордых — Our souls are drenched with the scorn of the arrogant and the contempt of the proud.

reading.ru: Ради дома Господа нашего Бога желаю блага тебе, Иерусалим.
reading.question: For whose sake does the psalmist wish good to Jerusalem?
options: For the sake of the house of the Lord our God
For the sake of his own family
For the sake of his own prosperity
For the sake of the king
reading.correct: For the sake of the house of the Lord our God
reading.explain: The verse states: Ради дома Господа нашего Бога желаю блага тебе, Иерусалим — For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I will seek your good.
